tagline: Over the Smokies by the gap somebody found late.
intro: Out of Gatlinburg, US 441 climbs the Tennessee side of the Smokies on stone bridges and walls from the 1930s and early 1940s, up the pronounced curves into the spruce-fir forest at Newfound Gap on the state line. Beyond the gap it goes on down into North Carolina to Cherokee, 31 miles in all from Gatlinburg, and never once leaves the national park.

The gap was the late find. For a long time the lowest way over was taken to be Indian Gap, two miles west, where an arduous unpaved road had run since 1839. In 1872 Arnold Guyot measured the mountains and found this one lower. The highway came over it in 1932.

moments.title: Chimney Tops
moments.text: One of the few bare rock summits in the Smokies, a double knob the Cherokee called the forked antler. Its trail leaves the road about seven miles above Sugarlands.

moments.title: Newfound Gap
moments.text: At 5,048 feet the road, the state line and the Appalachian Trail all cross the gap. Franklin Roosevelt dedicated the park here, at the Rockefeller Memorial, in 1940.

moments.title: Kuwohi
moments.text: Seven miles up a side road, a 1959 concrete tower with a spiral ramp stands on the highest point in Tennessee, 6,643 feet, in spruce-fir forest.

practical: The road is kept open all year except during and just after winter storms, when it may close for hours. Park rules allow plows and a gravel-sand mix but no chemicals. Parking at Kuwohi often fills.
